extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing stand-up comedians; comedy students and performers
extracted.subtask_description: Glossary-style practical guidance and standards for writing, rehearsing, and performing stand-up comedy, including timing, joke structure, stagecraft, and club etiquette. Useful for comedians developing material and stage technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: headliner
rubrics_metrics.description: The third and last comedian (main act) who has a following and performs 45–60 minutes to close shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role/expectation: ability to attract audience, sustain a long set; see opener, middle, closer.

rubrics_metrics.name: heckler
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience members who talk out loud or make comments and interrupt shows and the comedian's rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: usually drunk or high; must be managed to preserve rhythm. See heckler line, rip.

rubrics_metrics.name: heckler line
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-prepared insult jokes to use on different kinds of hecklers to get them to shut up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: memorize witty comebacks; can convert interruption into a comedic moment. See insult, comeback, put down.

rubrics_metrics.name: host (MC / emcee / compere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedian responsible for opening the show, introducing performers, keeping energy up, and often performing material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties include warming crowd, transitions, housekeeping; skill: crowd management and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: housekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties of the MC to make announcements, promote shows, recognize birthdays, point out exits/restrooms, calm hecklers, sell merch, run raffles, give curtain calls, and end shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: make necessary but brief announcements before starting; keeps show running smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurry a joke / rush a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering a joke faster than audience can process the setup→punchline relationship, diminishing or killing the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: mistrust of material leads to hurrying; remedy: allow processing time and pauses. See processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: hurt line
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective tipping point when the pain in the comedy becomes real and turns mood into drama; a sharp, cutting remark intended to sting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk: can stun the room before laughter; be aware of emotional threshold and consequences (e.g., cruelty). See dramedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting out impersonations of recognizable celebrities for comic effect or political satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: recognizable mannerisms/voice; ethical considerations re: targets. See impersonations.

rubrics_metrics.name: improv / improvisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spontaneous creation of bits and sketches not planned beforehand; working with troupe fundamentals and improv games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for crowd work and riffing; related to ad-lib and crowd interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: inside joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor based on shared knowledge known only by a select group or institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: limits audience comprehension; use carefully or tailor to audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: intro / introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prewritten announcement by an MC about performers as they come on stage; often comical and intended to get a laugh within first seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: make intros funny to set tone and warm the crowd; opening line should get a laugh in the first 15 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke (one-liner model)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single unit of humor typically composed of Setup and Punchline linked by a Connector; Setup establishes a Target Assumption and Punchline gives a Reinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 5 mechanisms (Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation, 1st/2nd story) per Greg Dean; study joke structure to fix and write jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual device by Greg Dean illustrating his model of joke structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to identify where jokes are failing and to guide rewriting; see joke structure and Joke Prospector Writing System.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke file
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of jokes organized and stored (index cards or digital) for development and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: maintain a centralized joke file to keep material accessible and track versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Map
rubrics_metrics.description: First part of Greg Dean's Joke Prospector Writing System: starts with a topic, creates punch-premise, setup-premise, and produces series of joke setups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as structured ideation to define topic and generate setups before mining punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Mine
rubrics_metrics.description: Second part of Greg Dean's system: uses Joke Map setups and applies five mechanisms (Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation) to write punchlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-oriented guidance for turning setups into working punchlines; part of a step-by-step writing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke premise / punch-premise / setup-premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that provides the message or position from which jokes or routines are written; punch-premise is negative opinion, setup-premise is positive/opposite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use premise to focus writing; punch-premise informs the joke's stance; see Joke Map and Joke Mine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Prospector Writing System
rubrics_metrics.description: Greg Dean's two-part system (Joke Map + Joke Mine) to teach step-by-step one-liner writing beginning with a topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimed as a complete system for writing one-liners; recommended reading for structural learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke structure (Greg Dean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model with two sections (Setup, Punchline) linked by five mechanisms: 1st Story, Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation, 2nd Story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the model to identify and fix jokes; locate Target Assumption and Reinterpretation; refer to Step by Step to Stand-Up Comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: joke writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of crafting humorous expressions across improvisation, drafting, rewriting, punching up scripts, and pitching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes broad activities from improvising to editing; sign-up for classes or read targeted books to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: jokey (cliché jokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious or cliché jokes or a performance that sounds written and unnatural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: avoid writing material that reads as 'jokey'—aim for natural speech and originality. See hack.

rubrics_metrics.name: kick ass / kill (success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing such that the audience laughs loud and often; 'killing' implies continuous laughter through the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal metric of successful performance; linked to LPMs and audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill a laugh / step on laughs / talk over laughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions after delivering a joke that stop or reduce laughter (continuing to speak, miswording, bad timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipatterns to avoid—pause to let laughter peak; don't talk over laughs; take a beat after punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: laser beam
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics, premises, routines, or characters that set off public controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness: controversial material can generate attention but risks backlash; be prepared for consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: laughs per minute (LPMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement counting number of laughs in routines or shows; used as a performance metric (e.g., professional level = 5 LPMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LPMs as a quantitative metric to evaluate and refine material and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: light / the light / red light / respect the light
rubrics_metrics.description: Signal(s) indicating time remaining or that performance time is up; red light is final strongest signal to end immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Etiquette: respect the light or risk being cut off/forced off stage; adjust set length accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: lineup / show list / set list
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered list of comedians and time slots or bullet-point reminders of joke order for a show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice with a set list to manage transitions and pacing; know your position on the lineup.

rubrics_metrics.name: lottery / sign ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems for determining open mic lineups (names drawn from a hat/bucket) or pre-sign up with later lottery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand venue signup policies to secure stage time; strategy varies by venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: material conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple comedians in the same lineup have similar topics, premises, or jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overlapping material in showcases; tailor or alter material if conflicts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: MC
rubrics_metrics.description: Master or Mistress of Ceremonies: person who introduces performers and manages show flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skillset includes housekeeping, stretch, and transitions between acts; may perform as opener-MC.

rubrics_metrics.name: merch / merchandise
rubrics_metrics.description: Souvenirs sold to augment income (t-shirts, caps, posters, CDs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: set up merch table to boost earnings and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: meta joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes that make fun of other common-knowledge jokes or familiar joke templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can subvert expectations; unfamiliar audiences may miss meta humor—consider tailoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: mic / microphone / mic stand / mic cord / mic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardware and technique for using microphone, stand, and cord to enhance communication and transitions onstage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: develop effective mic technique (holding/moving) to support delivery and smooth get-ons/offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: middle / opener / opener-MC / feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions in a traditional three-comedian lineup (opener first, middle second, headliner last); opener-MC also hosts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand role expectations and set length for each slot; adapt energy and material accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: monologist / monologue
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo comedian speaking from Narrator POV without acting out scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style: rely on narration and one-liners rather than scene acting; suitable for certain voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator POV / Self POV / Character POV / POV shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Three perceptual positions in storytelling: Narrator (direct to audience), Self (portraying self in scenes), Character (portraying others); POV shifts change staging and joke distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use POVs to stage scenes; storytelling requires shifting between POVs for acting and comic effect. See Anatomy of Funny Storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neurolinguistic Programming (NLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology for modeling outstanding performances and understanding how people organize thinking and language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used for personal development and modeling comedic performance techniques; optional tool, not core craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: on the road / road comic / road work / road agent or manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Work involving traveling to gigs outside home city; road agent/manager books and arranges appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience: road work builds stage time and resilience; logistics require booking and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: one-liners / one-liner timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short jokes using setup and punchline; timing involves waiting for laugh peak and pausing (count of 2–4) before next setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: let laugh peak then pause; tag timing matters for chaining laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: one-nighter
rubrics_metrics.description: A stand-up show that runs for only one night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: often used in touring and festival circuits; adapt set to single-date audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: open mic / open micer
rubrics_metrics.description: Venues where anyone can perform a few minutes; open micers are aspiring comedians who frequent them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open mics to get stage time, try material, and read room; formats vary by venue (lottery, sign-ups).

rubrics_metrics.name: opening line
rubrics_metrics.description: First joke of a show intended to get a laugh within the first fifteen seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: craft a strong opener to establish tone and secure early momentum; relates to LPMs and BCAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: oxymoron / paraprosdokian
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures of speech used as comedic devices (contradictory terms or surprising sentence endings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhetorical devices for cleverness and surprise; examples: George Carlin’s 'Military intelligence.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PA / PA system / PA representation
rubrics_metrics.description: PA = personal appearance or public address; PA system amplifies sound; PA representation books personal appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical: check PA system at venue early; representation helps with booking paid work.

rubrics_metrics.name: paid regular / regulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians selected by club management to perform frequently and get paid; regulars appear often (sometimes unpaid) to build material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role expectations: consistent quality and fit with venue; can be pathway to more stage time.

rubrics_metrics.name: pause / take a beat
rubrics_metrics.description: Silence after a punchline to allow laughter and processing, or between setup and punchline to build tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential timing tool; misuse (not pausing) can kill laughs. See timing, take a beat, break.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV (point of view)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for points of view (Narrator, Self, Character) used in staging and storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use POV distribution to place Setup, Punchline, and Tag across roles in storytelling vs one-liners.

rubrics_metrics.name: premise / routine premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Idea or statement (often negative for punch-premise) from which jokes or a routine are developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use premise to focus material and generate setups/punches; routine premise supports longer bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: preview / showcase / showcase clubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats/special shows for being seen by bookers/agents or for student previews; showcase clubs use long lineups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showcase strategy: tailor material for industry viewers and prepare multiple minutes of polished material.

rubrics_metrics.name: prop comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comics who use gadgets and props for jokes (e.g., Gallagher, Carrot Top).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance style: props define pacing and staging; audience expectation differs from one-liners/storytellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: public domain (as applied to topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics and premises are not owned; individual jokes have natural copyright but are hard to legally enforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/legal: assume topics are fair game; be aware that proving infringement is difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: punch / punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch = short for punchline; punchline communicates the Reinterpretation that makes the Target Assumption wrong; intended to shock/surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement: reveal near or at end of punchline; shorten punchlines when needed to increase impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: punch up / punch down
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch up: make jokes about higher-status targets; punch down: target lower-status people/institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical guideline: punching up generally safer/seen as fair; punching down risks cruelty and audience backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: punch-premise / Setup-Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps in the Joke Map: punch-premise = statement with a negative opinion; setup-premise = opposite positive opinion to seed setups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these structured steps for systematic joke generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: quip
rubrics_metrics.description: Witty clever often-taunting remark; now often replaced by 'wit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style note: quips function like insult/put down; avoid overuse to prevent jokey tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: read on material
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing jokes and judging audience responses (laughter/groans/boos/silence/applause) to adjust script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential iterative process: test, note responses, rewrite, and refine based on audience feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: real audience
rubrics_metrics.description: An audience composed of actual customers, not just comedians waiting to perform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance reality: test material with real audiences for honest feedback; comedians-only rooms give skewed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: red light / run the light
rubrics_metrics.description: Final signal to end immediately; running the light (ignoring it) may lead to being removed or banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Etiquette: do not continue after red light; respect club policies to maintain bookings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearsal Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Greg Dean's method of turning jokes/routines into scenes by acting them out (Narrator, Self, Character POVs) so material is remembered in pictures, sounds, feelings rather than rote words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: rehearse in scenes to avoid improper rehearsal (mere repetition) which codes jokes into self-talk and reduces natural delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinterpretation / reinterpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five joke mechanisms: the unexpected interpretation of the Connector expressed by the punchline; listing alternative reinterpretations during writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing technique: generate multiple reinterpretations as options for punchlines; put reveal near punchline end.

rubrics_metrics.name: reveal
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific information (word/phrase/action) that communicates the Reinterpretation; best placed near or at the end of the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement and economy: a tight reveal maximizes surprise; avoid muddying the reveal with extraneous words.

rubrics_metrics.name: rhythm of three / rule of three
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke format listing two positive items then a third negative/unexpected item that creates humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common format—use for set ups; examples demonstrate how to craft the third element as the funny twist.

rubrics_metrics.name: riff
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique in crowd work where comedian takes an audience idea and embellishes it to find humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill: requires listening and quick associative thinking; can produce large laughs when successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: rim shot
rubrics_metrics.description: Percussive sting (drum hits + cymbal) to punctuate an obvious joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly; often indicates an obvious punchline or groaner.

rubrics_metrics.name: rip
rubrics_metrics.description: To attack/insult or verbally tear into an audience member or comic (often a heckler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk: aggressive ripping can escalate situations; use calibrated comebacks/heckler lines instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: roast
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes used to playfully insult specific people/celebrities as a form of honor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format expectation: targets expect to be insulted; tone differs from general stand-up; see Roast Battle.

rubrics_metrics.name: roll
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering a string of jokes and tags that cause continuous laughter for an extended period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for sustained momentum through well-placed tags and timing; practice pacing to maintain the roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: routine / routine premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of jokes, act-outs, and tags on same topic/premise forming a sustained bit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure routines around a clear premise; use scene work and tags to extend laughs and maintain cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: running gag / callback
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes recurring two or more times within the same routine or show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use callbacks to reward attentive audiences and build cumulative laughs; don't overuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: rush a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as hurry a joke; communicating a joke too fast for audience processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation: slow down, trust setup, allow processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: sandwich / hammocking
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing weaker material or improvisation between two strong jokes; hammock metaphor balances a weaker joke between stronger ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique for transitions and protecting weaker bits—ensure support beams (strong jokes) flank weaker material.

rubrics_metrics.name: scene work / storytelling with scene work
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting up scenes and acting them out using Self and Character POVs to portray roles for comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires acting, staging, tenses, and psychology; integrates with Anatomy of Funny Storytelling for vivid delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: scream
rubrics_metrics.description: The loudest, most powerful instant laugh—indicative of a very strong joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A desirable reaction; can be targeted by high-impact punchlines or physical bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: segue
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional sentences or phrases that lead from one joke to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to preserve flow and avoid awkward topic jumps; well-crafted segues conceal editing and maintain momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: self talk
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal rehearsal method where a comedian memorizes words only (Broca area coding), leading to less natural recall onstage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid improper rehearsal by practicing in scenes and sensations to recall performance naturally rather than rote words.

rubrics_metrics.name: set / set list / show list
rubrics_metrics.description: A performance or list of jokes/routines to be performed; set can mean both the material and the act of repeating same words/body language each time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a set list to manage order; rehearse nuances so repeat performances are fresh, not mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: setup / Connector / Target Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: First part of a joke designed to misdirect by establishing the Target Assumption via the Connector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity in setup is essential to enable the reinterpretation; rewrite setups to make misdirection clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: showcase clubs / preview
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs that feature long lineups or special shows intended for bookers, students, or industry viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target material appropriate for industry visibility; polish minutes and prepare to be seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: shtick / sight gag / spit take
rubrics_metrics.description: Shtick = comic scene or gimmick; sight gag = visual joke; spit take = physical reaction gag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical/comedic devices require staging and practice; align with venue and performer strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: smooth on and smooth off
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for getting on and off stage to ensure well-run shows (phrase coined by Jerry Seinfeld).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stagecraft: rehearse entrances/exits and respect timing to maintain professionalism and return invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: spotlights / stage lights
rubrics_metrics.description: Lighting that affects visibility and performer comfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrive early to check lights; adapt performance if lights are too bright/dim.

rubrics_metrics.name: stage time
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of time a comedian gets to perform at a show; also refers to the experience gained onstage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize accumulating stage time to develop material and craft; manage allotted minutes carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: stay in the bit
rubrics_metrics.description: After delivering a Punchline, stop talking and remain in the same emotion/state as the joke to give space for laughter and keep momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique credited to Jerry Seinfeld; prevents stepping on laughs and preserves rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step by Step to Stand-Up Comedy (book)
rubrics_metrics.description: Greg Dean’s book laying out fundamental skills and techniques for becoming a comedian, with companion workbooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended resource for systematic learning of joke structure, rehearsal, and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: step on laughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing to speak or act after a punchline in a way that causes the audience to stop laughing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid by taking appropriate pauses; editing delivery reduces stepping on laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: stool
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical stage furniture allowing the comedian to sit during performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prop choice affects intimacy and pacing; use intentionally for bits needing sitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: story jokes / storytelling / storytelling joke structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer jokes or routines told as stories from Narrator POV with scene work; require scene acting, staging, and emotional detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More demanding than one-liners—requires acting, POV shifts, tenses, and timing; distribute setup/punch/tag across POVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: storytelling without scene work
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling stories from Narrator POV only, explaining scenes rather than acting them out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler storytelling approach; may rely more on descriptive language than physical acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: stretch
rubrics_metrics.description: When MCs must continue entertaining the audience until a technical or logistical problem is solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill: ability to ad-lib and hold the room during delays; keep energy and attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended result of a punchline—causing an unexpected reinterpretation that yields laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reveals to maximize surprise while maintaining clarity of setup and connector.

rubrics_metrics.name: tag / tag line
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional short punchline immediately following a punchline that does not require a new setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tags to extend laughs and build rolls; tag timing is critical to avoid overextending a laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: tailor
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting or altering material to fit unique performing situations and different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: adapt references and jokes to audience demographics (e.g., cops) to increase relatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: take / take a beat
rubrics_metrics.description: Facial reaction (take) or a pause (take a beat) used to express feeling or allow timing between lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use physical takes and beats strategically to shape timing and audience reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: talk over laughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing to speak during audience laughter, thereby interrupting and reducing the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern—avoid by practicing pause and staying in the bit; trust the laugh cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: talking head
rubrics_metrics.description: Comics who memorize words and deliver them with no emotion or physical movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: rehearse using Rehearsal Process and POV acting to bring material to life rather than rote delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target / Target Assumption / TCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Target = butt of joke (short for Target Assumption). Target Assumption is the expected interpretation of the Connector established by the Setup; TCR = Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core structural elements—identify target and craft connector/reinterpretation pair to land the joke; use TCR as shorthand during writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCR (Target Assumption, Connector, Reinterpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviation summarizing Greg Dean's core joke structure components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TCR as a checklist during joke writing and editing to ensure each part is present and clear.
